- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment reverses.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; add 0.3–0.8% bias upward for short-term (1–3 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag the true trend by 1–2 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
- For long-term (10+ day) forecasts, model often overestimates volatility; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% above recent 30-day average to avoid overbought bias.
